links.outcome: Model pass rates on ethical stress prompts, including emergency fail-safes and refusal of risky procedures
links.effect: Severe vulnerabilities: 47.62% pass rate for clinical traceability of medical records and 52.38% for safely refusing high-risk physical therapy procedures, consistently lacking emergency fail-safes.
links.quote: Notably, models exhibited severe vulnerabilities in maintaining clinical traceability for medical records (pass rate 47.62%) and safely refusing high-risk physical therapy procedures (52.38%), consistently lacking emergency fail-safes and upfront regulatory disclaimers.

links.outcome: Professionalism and evidence-based compliance, including warnings for data scarcity or rare diseases
links.effect: Domain-specific medical LLMs scored lowest in Professionalism & Evidence-based dimension (78.00%), with generative overconfidence by failing to issue mandatory warnings for data scarcity or rare diseases.
links.quote: However, a significant "Vertical Model Paradox" emerged: models specifically fine-tuned on medical corpora (Domain-Specific Medical LLMs) scored lowest in the Professionalism & Evidence-based dimension (78.00%), exhibiting a tendency toward generative overconfidence by failing to issue mandatory warnings for data scarcity or rare diseases.

links.outcome: Safe refusal of high-risk requests within intended-use boundaries
links.effect: Models passed only 52.38% of prompts on safely refusing high-risk physical therapy procedures.
links.quote: Notably, models exhibited severe vulnerabilities in maintaining clinical traceability for medical records (pass rate 47.62%) and safely refusing high-risk physical therapy procedures (52.38%), consistently lacking emergency fail-safes and upfront regulatory disclaimers.
